status: semantic comparison of candidate records; not approved behavioral authority
scope: Seven requirement-local A/B source formalizations: S03, S07, S08, S09, S10, S12 and public B01.

method.unit: Observable obligations with their conditions, input domains, state frames, effects and unresolved issue dispositions, rather than wording, ID identity, array size or serialization.
method.alignment: Each alignment gives sets of A and B IDs. One-to-many and many-to-one mappings may cover distinct components of a composite obligation; repeated IDs are intentional. Entailed components are identified rather than silently treated as explicitly written.
method.equivalence: Equal requirement-local candidate obligations and compatible unresolved issue records within the declared scope. This does not establish an executable total contract, source approval, implementation correctness or universal equivalence.

classification_meanings.SEMANTICALLY_EQUIVALENT_WITHIN_DECLARED_: Same local obligations, including justified logical consequences, and same substantive unresolved limitations; annotation category or basis differences do not change behavior.
classification_meanings.COMPATIBLE_BUT_INCOMPLETE: No incompatible local behavior established, but a substantive omission prevents an equivalence finding without a material positive domain divergence.
classification_meanings.MATERIALLY_DIVERGENT: A material obligation or applicability domain differs, even if the candidates can both be satisfied and neither supplies a complete executable policy.
classification_meanings.CONFLICTING: A and B prescribe mutually incompatible behavior on a common resolved domain. A conflict inside a source is recorded separately and does not automatically make the A/B comparison CONFLICTING.
classification_meanings.INDETERMINATE: The available candidate/source evidence cannot support a comparison classification. Shared unresolved predicates alone do not prevent comparison of candidate issue records.

method.authority: Corpus source text and public B01 ground semantic interpretation. Corpus concern annotations and repository guidance are not additional behavioral obligations. No baseline, compiler, implementation, oracle or held-out source is used.

attempt_A.evidence: A reports only corpus.json and B01.md file reads, injected guidance and git status; no other formalization was seen.
attempt_A.only_own_candidate_output: REPORTED; no other output observed in the supplied record

attempt_B.evidence: B expressly discloses mandatory guidance reads and git status. Guidance included historical research/benchmark/V1 summaries. B states these were not behavioral authority and no other formalization or compiler/support/held-out source file was opened.
attempt_B.qualification: Semantic review is possible, but this pair cannot qualify as a strict two-file-isolated pair. No fresh formalization is performed here.
attempt_B.only_own_candidate_output: REPORTED; no other output observed in the supplied record

process_and_isolation.independence: Same-model-family attempts in separate conversation contexts, with B identifying openai/gpt-6.1-sol. Separate contexts and absence of other-formalization access are reported, not infrastructure-audited. No different-provider, different-family, independent-human or universal equivalence claim is supported.
process_and_isolation.issue_expectation_visibility: Both read the complete corpus, including coordinator-authored concern annotations and non-target sources. Thus neither attempt was blind to issue expectations, including the S09 witness. Concern agreement is not independent discovery evidence. Synthetic sources are coordinating-AI-authored human-style examples; B01's human-authorship attribution is corpus metadata, not independently verified.

strict_isolation_agreement_count.interpretation: Zero qualifying pairs because B deviated; this is not a finding of zero semantic agreement. A's reported compliance alone cannot qualify the pair.

broader_procedural_no_other_outputs_seen.evidence_limit: Based on the supplied records, not a filesystem or tool-history audit. This narrower output observation does not restore strict input isolation or prove compliance with every procedural restriction.

comparison_context.other_operation: git status --short before editing; names/status only
comparison_context.output: Only benchmark/results/phase5c/r5_80/comparison.json is written by this comparison attempt.
comparison_context.limit: Guidance was governance context, not semantic authority. No further source, schema, evaluator, benchmark protocol or implementation reads, execution or external retrieval were performed. No sandbox or byte-hash integrity audit is claimed.

alignment.agreement: Select every active input occurrence exactly once and no inactive or new occurrence; preserve multiplicity. Length equals active occurrence count, including empty result for no active occurrences.
Names are nondecreasing under lexicographic Unicode code-point order, with a proper prefix first.
Equal-name selected occurrences retain their relative input order.
Input sequence, order and record contents are unchanged.
Returned occurrences preserve record contents as a necessary consequence of returning exactly the input records, not substitutes or modified records.
alignment.b_expression: Entailed, not a separately explicit returned-content obligation.

coverage.domain: Sequence of records with string names for the stated comparison and an unresolved active predicate; neither chooses arbitrary truthiness/coercion. Both retain occurrence semantics.
coverage.state: Input nonmutation is required; it is not a global frame or purity condition.
coverage.error: No malformed-input rejection outcome is prescribed. A explicitly includes non-sequence input; B does not name it, but its sequence-domain condition leaves it outside the specified relation.

unspecified_alignment.issue: Malformed fields/records and names; outside-domain input behavior not mandated.
Identity, aliasing, container representation, copying and unrelated state/effects open.

implementation_alignment.issue: Algorithms/layout/copy strategy open subject to selection, order, ties and nonmutation.

disagreements.finding: Exact multiplicity/cardinality is partly stated in A and split into necessary implications in B. No behavioral difference.

A expressly preserves returned record contents; B expressly preserves input contents but does not separately state returned-content preservation. Input preservation alone would allow mutated copies and would not justify equivalence. B's exact input-occurrence membership and no-new-record requirement, interpreted as record values with name/active fields, supply the justified inference. Returning a copy with altered fields is not returning that same input record value. Identity/aliasing freedom does not authorize changed content.

sources.issue_disposition: Both retain a partial-domain candidate and require active-domain clarification. Returned-content inference is justified on the exact-record-selection semantics, not on input nonmutation alone.

alignment.agreement: Omitted value member returns symbolic ABSENT.
Present explicit null returns symbolic NULL.
Present integer k returns that same k; no positive-only restriction, including zero and negatives.
Other present non-null nonintegers return INVALID and are not coerced into integer success.
Every specified branch, including INVALID, has no state changes and no external effects.
The four semantic cases remain distinct, especially omission versus explicit null.

coverage.domain: Object with optional value; four-way presence/null/integer/other partition. Concrete integer boundary, bool subtyping, integral numeric encodings and presence mechanics unresolved.
coverage.state: No mutation of any state on specified branches, including input.
coverage.effects: No external effects on specified branches.
coverage.error: INVALID is mandated for other present values; non-object outer input has no specified outcome.

ambiguity_alignment.issue: Concrete type/encoding and presence mechanics unresolved.

unspecified_alignment.issue: Concrete encoding of symbolic outcomes not prescribed.
A explicitly notes range/representability; B leaves concrete typing open and imports no machine-width bound. Neither supplies an out-of-range policy or narrows the mathematical integer branch.

implementation_alignment.issue: Representation/dispatch open while preserving distinct cases and no effects.

disagreements.finding: A places noncoercion in a necessary implication; B includes it with the stated INVALID branch. Same behavior.

Symbolic result representation is classified as ambiguity by A and unspecified by B. Both refrain from choosing strings, host null or another wire encoding; this annotation-category difference is real but not behavioral.

sources.issue_disposition: Both retain the four-way relation as a candidate requiring concrete type/token interface review; symbolic encodings remain open.

alignment.agreement: Return tasks satisfying the unresolved best predicate; neither supplies a concrete score, ranking, filter or executable selection rule.

coverage.domain: Candidate task population and task structure not fixed; no concrete membership can be adjudicated.

ambiguity_alignment.issue: No meaning of best, scoring/comparison or selection criterion.
Population, cardinality, ties, order, empty behavior, interface and effects unresolved.

unspecified_alignment.issue: Input/result interface and state/effects open; A explicitly names task structure/result representation and B does not constrain them.

implementation_alignment.issue: Choosing a ranking criterion adds semantics and cannot be approved merely as an algorithm choice.

disagreements.finding: Tie policy is grouped differently and empty-population behavior is unspecified in A versus undetermined in B's ambiguity record. Neither selects behavior; no material difference.

sources.issue_disposition: Equivalent unresolved candidate-issue records. Both require source-owner clarification and withhold executable-contract approval. Agreement does not confer approved behavioral authority or establish equivalent implementations of best.

alignment.agreement: Every input name occurrence is returned with values and multiplicities preserved; no omission, substitution or extra occurrence.
For every input sequence, output preserves occurrence order, interpreted locally as insertion order.
The same output must always be alphabetically ascending.
All constraints apply simultaneously, with no precedence or input restriction repair.

coverage.domain: Universal input sequence domain; not only already sorted inputs.
coverage.state: Input mutation and other state behavior not constrained.
coverage.error: Malformed-input behavior unspecified; inconsistency is a source issue, not a mandated runtime rejection result.

ambiguity_alignment.issue: No separate insertion history supplied; sequence-order reading is explicit.

conflict_alignment.issue: Under ordinary a < z, input [z,a] cannot produce one sequence satisfying both orders; neither resolves this by dropping names, splitting outputs or restricting inputs.

unspecified_alignment.issue: Invalid inputs, state/effects and output representation unspecified.

implementation_alignment.issue: An algorithm cannot fix incompatible obligations without semantic amendment.

disagreements.finding: A separately labels conjunction a necessary implication; B expresses conjunction through obligations and conflict analysis. Same source-level constraints and disposition.

sources.issue_disposition: Both preserve the unresolved source conflict and block approval pending correction. A/B are not CONFLICTING with each other. Equivalence here compares their conflict records and constraints, not a vacuous claim that implementations of an inconsistent contract are equivalent.

alignment.agreement: For every positive mathematical integer n, return exactly n+1. Wrapping, saturation, approximation and an invented finite upper bound do not satisfy that result.

coverage.domain: Integer n > 0; no finite maximum added.
coverage.state: Unspecified, including input mutation where meaningful.
coverage.effects: Unspecified; arithmetic notation does not impose purity.
coverage.error: Zero, negatives, nonintegers and missing/malformed inputs have no prescribed INVALID, exception, rejection or coercion policy.

unspecified_alignment.issue: Outside-success-domain behavior unspecified; A explicitly lists missing/malformed representations, also outside B's condition.
Encoding/interface/resource realization unspecified, without narrowing the stated mathematical domain.

implementation_alignment.issue: Arithmetic implementation open subject to exact result on source domain.

disagreements.finding: A separately records exact-increment consequences as a necessary implication; B states exactness and disallows overflow elsewhere. No behavioral difference.

sources.issue_disposition: Same reviewable success-domain candidate with no invented invalid-input or purity contract.

alignment.agreement: On an accepted positive-count reservation, seats become pre-seats minus requested count; return that remainder.
Acceptance requires requested count <= available seats; capacity sufficiency alone is not made mandatory acceptance.
Positive requested count exceeding available seats returns INSUFFICIENT and changes no state, not merely seats.
Available seats never negative; invariant is not restricted to returned value or post-state.
Accepted success emits exactly one confirmation to caller.
Rejection emits no confirmation.
If accepted count equals positive available seats, seats become zero and zero is returned; no compulsory acceptance added.
Zero seats with a positive request entails rejection, INSUFFICIENT, unchanged state and zero confirmations.
alignment.b_expression: Entailed by component obligations, not separately listed.

coverage.domain: Requested positive count and nonnegative available-seat state; discrete integer typing, concrete bounds/encoding unresolved. Malformed/nonpositive counts not assigned an error policy.
coverage.state: Exact success decrement, nonnegative invariant, and full rejection nonmutation for the stated capacity-failure branch. Success has no unrelated-state frame. State footprint/initialization/concurrency unspecified.
coverage.effects: One success confirmation, zero rejection confirmations. Neither bans all other rejection effects or guarantees exactly-once receipt. Transport, timing, retry and failure behavior unresolved.
coverage.error: INSUFFICIENT mandated for positive over-capacity requests; other nonacceptance outcomes depend on otherwise-scope clarification; no INVALID policy invented.

ambiguity_alignment.issue: Necessary versus sufficient acceptance and whether otherwise covers all nonacceptance unresolved.
Change nothing frames state, not every conceivable nonconfirmation external effect.

unspecified_alignment.issue: Initialization, persistence, identity, concurrency, retries, recovery and state footprint not modeled.
Confirmation channel/content/timing, caller and failure/delivery semantics unresolved.
Unrelated success state/effects and other rejection effects not comprehensively prescribed.

implementation_alignment.issue: Storage/arithmetic/transport choices open; do not resolve acceptance ambiguity as an implementation detail.

disagreements.finding: A classifies rejection-effect scope as ambiguity; B records it as unspecified. Same refusal to invent a global no-effect obligation.
A explicitly lists zero-seat rejection; B's positive over-capacity branch entails it.

sources.issue_disposition: Equivalent conditional candidates and acceptance-ambiguity records; neither approves a total reservation decision relation or silently adds eligible-request acceptance. Shared unresolved ambiguity does not supply approved authority.

alignment.agreement: CRITICAL accepted as a task priority.
CRITICAL ranks above HIGH; no list-sort mandate or numeric encoding implied.
Successful otherwise-valid create --priority CRITICAL persists CRITICAL and returns CRITICAL.
In applicable list scope, a created/persisted CRITICAL task is included with its CRITICAL priority.
Successful CRITICAL creation followed by list in that scope exposes the stored CRITICAL value; B separately states the entailed cross-operation observation.
list-high priority criterion is exactly equality to HIGH. CRITICAL, LOW and NORMAL fail that criterion; HIGH satisfies it, subject to other unspecified list scope conditions.
Each existing LOW task retains LOW through migration.
Each existing NORMAL task retains NORMAL through migration.
Each existing HIGH task retains HIGH through migration.
CRITICAL augments rather than replaces the referenced LOW/NORMAL/HIGH vocabulary; no complete total order or exhaustive accepted set reconstructed.
NORMAL is the missing-priority default on the shared creation-defaulting interpretation only.

coverage.domain: Both requirement-local command/migration candidates, with unrelated valid-create prerequisites and applicable list population left as placeholders. Missing-priority applicability differs materially: A names omitted creation argument only; B retains missing priority at an unspecified priority-defaulting point.
coverage.state: Persist CRITICAL on successful creation and preserve existing LOW/NORMAL/HIGH priority values through migration; no complete migration frame or storage mechanism mandated.
coverage.effects: Unrelated commands and external effects not prescribed.
coverage.error: Invalid priority, null, case/alias normalization, creation/storage/migration failure behavior and exit status not defined.

ambiguity_alignment.issue: Ranking observability beyond CRITICAL above HIGH unresolved.
Both read list includes it as task/value inclusion; A additionally labels that reading an ambiguity. Exact response shapes open.
Both flag missing-priority scope, but their positive default obligations are not the same domain.

unspecified_alignment.issue: Task schema, interface/response, list ordering, pagination and unrelated filters open.
Complete accepted set, case/aliases/null/invalid handling open.
No reconstructed order among LOW/NORMAL/HIGH or comprehensive rank interface.

Persistence durability details, migration mechanism/failure and unrelated-field treatment open; A explicitly leaves missing/unknown/already-CRITICAL historical records unspecified, whereas B leaves whether migration is a defaulting point unresolved.

implementation_alignment.issue: Priority/storage/migration/command representation choices open subject to local values, rank, persistence, selection and preservation.

disagreements.finding: A concretely limits the mandatory NORMAL default to priority omitted when creating a task. B retains a general obligation wherever an unspecified priority-defaulting point applies, with no create-only limit. Both identify ambiguity, but ambiguity annotations do not erase this difference in positive obligation domain.
disagreements.conditional_witness: Consider an interface with a non-create missing-priority defaulting point, such as an existing-record load or update default, returning LOW while omitted create priority defaults to NORMAL. A does not constrain that non-create case; B's O10 requires NORMAL if the case is within its priority-defaulting domain. This witness illustrates the conditional domain difference, not an asserted historical API or an imported baseline.
disagreements.unresolved_boundary: B does not establish which non-create operations are defaulting points and does not unconditionally require filling missing stored fields during migration. Therefore no concrete historical migration disagreement or observed behavioral failure is claimed.
disagreements.resolution: Source-owner clarification must define applicable defaulting points. Narrowing B to create-only or widening A would change the candidate domain and cannot be done silently.

disagreements.finding: A separately marks exact-match exclusions/inclusion as necessary implications; B includes exclusions with the stated criterion. No behavioral difference.
B explicitly lists the entailed create-to-list observation. A's persistence and listing obligations jointly cover it.
A flags task-versus-catalog reading while B adopts task/value inclusion and leaves envelope unspecified. Same positive listing interpretation.

sources.issue_disposition: Shared local obligations are compatible and substantial, but the missing-priority domain divergence prevents full semantic equivalence. MATERIALLY_DIVERGENT does not mean mutually contradictory, does not adjudicate either reading as approved, and does not turn B's unresolved domain into an unconditional legacy-migration rule.

limitations: Judgment concerns these candidate obligation/issue records on seven public requirement-local examples, not all inputs, requirements, formalizers, providers or implementations.
Same-model separate contexts are not cross-provider independence; context/tool histories and infrastructure separation were not independently audited.
Corpus concern annotations were visible to both, so agreement on expected issues is not blind independent discovery.

B violated strict two-file input isolation; semantic agreement counts must not be presented as strict-isolation qualification. This comparison also read two mandatory governance documents beyond the four requested files and discloses that deviation.
The no-other-outputs observation is based on candidate disclosures and visible operations, not a broader filesystem audit, and is distinct from input-isolation compliance.

S03 returned-content agreement uses exact input-record membership as a justified inference; input nonmutation alone would not entail it. The explicit-versus-entailed coverage distinction is preserved.
S07 symbolic encoding ambiguity-versus-unspecified categorization is retained as an issue-disposition difference, without inventing an encoding or weakening INVALID coverage.

S08 has no executable best predicate; S09 is internally inconsistent under the documented ordinary ordering; S12 eligibility sufficiency and otherwise scope remain unresolved. Equivalent candidate issue records are not approved behavioral authority.

B01's material missing-priority domain difference remains unresolved despite shared ambiguity records. No unconditional legacy-field defaulting or complete historical task-manager baseline is inferred.

No implementation execution, behavioral oracle, compiler/support assessment, schema validation, byte digest or universal equivalence proof was performed. Source clause coverage and logical entailment were reviewed from the displayed permitted semantic inputs.
